paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Ruth does exactly what Naomi tells her, and she does it quietly, at midnight, with no speech and no show. She says, "I will do everything you say" (Ruth 3:5), and then she does it (Ruth 3:6). I think that's a picture of trusting somebody wiser when you can't see how the whole plan ends.

Now look at what Boaz does with his midnight surprise. He says, "May the LORD bless you, my daughter," and he tells her not to be afraid (Ruth 3:10-11). He says the whole town knows she is "a woman of noble character" (Ruth 3:11). Then he tells her the truth, even when it complicates things: there is a nearer redeemer, and he won't pretend there isn't (Ruth 3:12). He promises that if that man doesn't want to redeem her, "as surely as the LORD lives, I will" (Ruth 3:13). That's a man who keeps his word, even when the details get complicated.

And then comes the part that hits me where I live, baker. Ruth goes home with her shawl full of barley, and Naomi tells her to wait, because Boaz "will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today" (Ruth 3:18). Waiting is hard work, and I should know, because I did a LOT of it in the dark. But you can do your part, trust good counsel, and then wait without panicking. This story isn't over, so hold on to that.
